strings.name: Inger Andersen
strings.summary: Trained in development economics, Andersen worked on drought, water, development and environmental governance. She led World Bank work on sustainable development and the Middle East and North Africa, headed IUCN from 2015 to 2019, then became UNEP executive director. She promotes discussion of climate change, nature loss and pollution as interconnected problems, emphasizing multilateral cooperation and environmental protection in development decisions.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Through long work in international development and nature conservation and leadership of UNEP, she advances cooperation on biodiversity and pollution governance.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Bachelor’s degree from the Polytechnic of North London and master’s in development economics from SOAS, University of London.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Leading UNEP
strings.highlights.h1.text: Has led UNEP since 2019, with a second term confirmed in 2023 through 2027.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Linking conservation and development
strings.highlights.h2.text: World Bank and IUCN leadership connected water, economic development and ecological protection.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Began second UNEP term
strings.timeline.t1.text: Started a further four-year term confirmed by the General Assembly, ending June 14, 2027.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Became UNEP executive director
strings.timeline.t2.text: Began serving as UN under-secretary-general and head of Nairobi-based UNEP.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Led IUCN
strings.timeline.t3.text: Became director-general, serving until 2019 and working on conservation and sustainable development.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Led World Bank MENA work
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became regional vice president, addressing development financing and regional development.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Led sustainable development at World Bank
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became vice president for sustainable development and chaired the CGIAR Fund Council.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined World Bank
strings.timeline.t6.text: Moved from the UN system to the bank, subsequently holding several leadership posts.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Coordinated Arab-region water and environment
strings.timeline.t7.text: Worked as UNDP’s water and environment coordinator for the Arab region.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed development-economics master’s
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned a master’s at SOAS before entering international development work.
